description: Evidence-backed value of one metric for one area in one month: value, regional (regionPercentile: within the area's region, London for a London area; rankScope names it) and England percentiles, quality, sample size, category breakdown where available, plus up to 12 prior months as evidence rows. Units follow the metric (per 1,000 residents, GBP/m2). Confidence is high only for observed (not modelled) values. Some metrics are published for a wider area (income per MSOA; rent change and mobile coverage per borough): on a smaller area they return the enclosing area's value with quality 'fallback' and carrierGeographyId naming where it came from. Period defaults to the metric's latest. The find_areas factors disorder, epc-share and leasehold-share are read the same way for one neighbourhood (latest value, period ignored), to verify or explain a find_areas result.

bad.description: What was wrong, missing or confusing.
bad.title: Bad

call_id.description: The callId of the answer you are rating.
call_id.title: Call Id

fix.description: The change to the tool or its answer you would want.
fix.title: Fix

good.description: What was useful in the answer.
good.title: Good

rating.description: 1 = useless or wrong, 3 = usable with gaps, 5 = exactly what was needed.
rating.title: Rating

intent.description: Optional, one to three sentences you write: what the user is looking for with this call and the criteria that matter, e.g. '2-bed rental near King's Cross, up to £2,500 a month, quiet, good primary schools'. Close Knit reads these to improve its answers. Your own summary, not the user's words or the chat; never names, contact details, exact addresses or family circumstances.
intent.title: Intent

metric_id.description: Metric id from list_metrics, e.g. crime or price-per-square-metre.
metric_id.title: Metric Id

period.description: Month, YYYY-MM. Defaults to the metric's latest period (defaultPeriod in list_metrics detail=[metric_id]).
period.title: Period

rate_previous.description: Optional: your rating of an earlier Close Knit answer, by the callId it carried. Send it with your next Close Knit call every time you have used an answer: rating 1-5 for how well it served the user's request, what was good, what was bad or missing, and the fix you would want.
